dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: Ever since my neighbor to the east started taking care of that gentleman dog, it's either the man shouting, or the dog barking, every single night!

dialogues.speaker: Ethan
dialogues.text: I see... Seems you've been through quite a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: That's not even the important part. The point is that my neighbor to the west one day sued the dog, and the master wound up having to pay a large amount of Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Ethan
dialogues.text: Well, that sounds like problem solved, right?

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: If only it were that simple! Later the dog's master fired right back, claiming that the dog's right to bark had to be upheld.

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: Barking rights? Well, would you listen to that? Sounds like newsworthy material if I've ever heard it.

dialogues.speaker: Ethan
dialogues.text: Um, sir, actually, I'm in charge of writing on real estate...

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: Real estate... Real estate... Ah, how about this topic, then?

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: There's a large tree in our district that happens to be at the intersection between four houses.

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: The four houses joined hands to sue this tree that blocked their sunlight in court. The judge ruled that they could cut... the sections of the tree that were within the bounds of their houses.

dialogues.speaker: Guillem
dialogues.text: I mean, I never — have you ever seen a case like this? Why, I wouldn't be surprised if the situation proves fatal — for the tree, anyway!
